whats_working.label: Issues the company did fix
whats_working.gloss: The healthy counter-pattern — the narrative acknowledges the problem was ultimately corrected.
whats_working.narrative: Interactions flagged under "resolution_acknowledged" reflect customers acknowledging that a partial resolution occurred, typically a subset of disputed charges being refunded, while the remainder were denied or unresolved. In each case the customer confirms receipt of some remediation but describes the outcome as incomplete, with additional charges left unaddressed, appeals denied, or accounts left negative or closed. The acknowledgment of partial refund is paired with a statement of dissatisfaction about the remaining unresolved amounts.

watch_list.label: Lockouts with no recovery path
watch_list.gloss: Customers locked out of the account and unable to get back in through the provider's own process.

watch_list.label: Disputed fees
watch_list.gloss: Fees or charges customers say were incorrect, undisclosed, or wrongly applied.

watch_list.label: Fraud victims turned away
watch_list.gloss: Scam and fraud victims whose claims were denied or redirected instead of resolved.

watch_list.label: Frozen funds and blocked accounts
watch_list.gloss: Customers cut off from their own money by a provider-side freeze or hold.

watch_list.label: Payments not credited
watch_list.gloss: Payments made but not applied — wrong account, wrong balance, or lost in processing.

watch_list.label: Refunds refused
watch_list.gloss: Customers who asked for their money back for a concrete loss and did not get it.

watch_list.label: Repeat complaints on unresolved issues
watch_list.gloss: The same issue raised before and still unresolved — the first response should have prevented this contact.

watch_list.label: Support that doesn't answer
watch_list.gloss: No human reachable, no reply, or only templated answers that don't address the issue.
